kilde: Policy and Practice in Health and Safety
sammendrag: In 2005, the Swedish Work Environment Authority inspected 1,721 workplaces in two days. The inspections were carried out as part of the Authority’s campaign to support the European Agency for Safety and Health at Work’s ‘European Week’ initiative on raising awareness of noise at work. To evaluate the effectiveness of the campaign, a web-based questionnaire was sent to inspected workplaces. The same questionnaire was sent to matched controls, ie workplaces that were not inspected but otherwise resembled, as far as possible, those that were inspected. The questionnaire included questions about whether specific types of measure against noise had been taken after the campaign. Large differences were found between inspected and uninspected workplaces. For example, plans of action against noise were seven times more common in inspected workplaces than in uninspected workplaces, exposure measurements five times more common, and measures to reduce noise more than twice as common. On average, inspected workplaces had implemented 2.5 types of action against noise after the campaign, whereas the controls had implemented only 0.8. The inspected workplaces also reported a higher degree of knowledge about new regulations concerning noise. Eighty-eight per cent of the inspected workplaces reported that the activities of the Authority were the reason for the actions they had taken against noise. The study shows that the inspection campaign was highly successful in getting organisations to introduce noise prevention measures.
tittel: Effects of Workplace Inspections: The Swedish Noise Campaign
